teaching_note: Distinguish wartime OSS records, later historical scholarship and the OSS Society's commemorative resource directory. These genres illuminate different questions: contemporary institutional intentions, retrospective interpretation and archive discovery. Organizational ancestry alone does not make wartime authorities or methods applicable to later CIA practice [@ageint128; @ageint129].
title: OSS in World War II

teaching_note: An announcement for a manual collection is discovery context, not an authenticated item-level manual. Establish original issuer, edition, publication date and release evidence before interpreting text; even authentic doctrine does not establish implementation. Examine historical authority and accountability without collecting intelligence or rehearsing clandestine procedures.
title: OSS Secret Intelligence Manual: historical provenance

teaching_note: A later institutional republication must be distinguished from the wartime provisional edition it reproduces: a provisional rule, later editor's introduction and historian's judgment are different evidence. 'Provisional' signals a document status to investigate, not proof of poor or effective practice. Compare provenance and stated institutional remit, not operational instructions [@ageint119].
title: OSS Provisional Basic Field Manual

teaching_note: The archival item can support its historical text and metadata, not a general success narrative for all special operations. Record document date separately from digitization and public-release dates, and distinguish wartime prescription from a later account of conduct. No mission planning, maritime techniques or operational reenactment is part of this lesson [@ageint118].
title: Special Operations Field Manual

teaching_note: A collection announcement does not authenticate a particular device catalog, establish deployment or measure effectiveness. The historical question concerns institutional responsibility, source provenance and civilian consequences, not construction, use or testing of devices. Leave technical and operational claims unsupported rather than filling them from a memorable title.
title: OSS Special Weapons and Devices: archival and ethical context

teaching_note: A preserved instruction is evidence that someone prescribed it, not that it was carried out or worked. Selection for modern republication can privilege novelty over historical representativeness. Study authorship, audience, release and accountability only; no sabotage instructions or workplace/service experiments are reproduced.
title: Simple Sabotage Field Manual (1944): historical limits

teaching_note: Separate a historical influence objective from actual audience response, and distinguish the manual from a modern announcement describing its availability. Rhetorical analysis can characterize a text but cannot diagnose an audience or infer durable effect. Compare intended practice with documented accountability, not covert message design.
title: Morale Operations Field Manual

teaching_note: The Senate's official retrospective distinguishes the FBI's COINTELPRO disruption of civil-rights/anti-war activity from NSA's SHAMROCK/MINARET communications monitoring; these are not interchangeable 'CIA operations' (https://www.senate.gov/about/powers-procedures/investigations/church-committee.htm). Its abuse–investigation–reform chronology records the committee's January 1975 creation, 29 April 1976 final report, the 1976 Senate intelligence committee and 1978 FISA, while its account of executive responses includes new guidelines and Executive Order 12036, later revoked in 1981. Tower's appended concern about unnecessarily restricting presidential discretion differs from the report's accountability conclusion; formal reform, dissent and demonstrated compliance are separate evidence cells. This inspected institutional retrospective establishes what the Senate historical account says, not that reforms ended abuses; the underlying Book I report remains a document-level lead, not a passage claimed read here [@public_church_committee_book_i_1976]. Compare rights harms and oversight limits alongside institutional achievements; ICD 203 alone supplies neither this history nor current legal authority.
title: CIA Cold War Operations: oversight, abuses and reform evidence

teaching_note: Distinguish Mulholland's reproduced text from later commentary and editorial claims about the CIA/MKULTRA context. Authenticity or historical institutional use would not establish legitimacy or effectiveness; consent and rights harms remain central historical questions. title: CIA Manual of Trickery and Deception (Mulholland): historical accountability

teaching_note: This 1995 Militia Free Press/The Resister publication is not a CIA or OSS institutional manual; placement beneath a Cold War CIA heading does not change its provenance. Its legitimate role here is a counterexample to attribution by adjacency, not evidence of U.S. government practice or endorsed resistance instruction [@ageint120].
title: Principles of Tradecraft: a private publication, not CIA doctrine

teaching_note: Separate record creation, internal circulation and later public release: ageint090's routing sheet and attached State report do not provide independent confirmation of the same report in another record. CIA archive custody does not make the State report or a hosted third-party assessment CIA-authored. The documents illuminate historical U.S. assessments, not automatically Soviet intent or actual persuasion effects [@ageint088; @ageint089; @ageint090; @ageint091].
title: Soviet Active Measures Documents (CREST Collection)

raw: 28.3 Studies in Intelligence: The CIA's Professional Journal[^131][^132][^133]
teaching_note: Completed offline oversight case: H1 is a synthetic 1976 investigation finding of inadequate authorization, H2 a 1978 institutional rule requiring prior review, H3 a 1990 retrospective asserting the problem ended, and H4 a catalog showing that only selected files were released in 2000. The completed chronology separates alleged-event date, finding date, rule date and release date: H1 supports the finding, H2 the formal rule, H3 an institutional interpretation, and H4 a selection limit; no record measures compliance after reform. Withheld H5 is a 1979 exception memo, so retract H3's universal success claim while retaining evidence of formal change; redacted reasons remain unknown, not proof of either guilt or innocence. The case-to-principle answer is reform adopted does not equal harm eliminated, and retrospective knowledge cannot be assigned to earlier decision-makers (see [@sec:analytic-workflow]); official journal articles likewise require author/genre and disclosure-context checks [@ageint131; @ageint132; @ageint133].
title: Studies in Intelligence: The CIA's Professional Journal

Distinguish the author's professional affiliation from institutional endorsement, and a plausible argument for continued human intelligence from a measured forecast. Do not convert historical human-source discussion into software-agent instruction [@ageint019; @ageint034].
title: Vol. 70, No. 1 (March 2026): "Espionage in Our AI Future" (Mulligan/RAND)
